lawyer:
Md. Monirujjaman (Rubel), DAG with Kazi Bazlur Rashid, AAG and Delwara Begum (Bela), AAG—For the State. 
Momtaz Begum, Advocate For the State Defence Lawyer.
parties:
State ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Younus Sarder ----- Condemned- Prisoner
full_judgment:
29. A pertinent question crops up— Does accused Younus Sarder's stayed together with deceased Zohura Khatun at the mother's house at the fateful night give rise to any presumption that the accused was involved in commission of offence? The answer of the aforesaid question is in the negative. Precisely speaking, it is the claim of the prosecution that the two months before the occurrence deceased along with her son came to the Ambaria village of PO house under Khoksa police station, under District Kushtia. Thereafter, the accused came to the PO house on 30-12-2006 at about 7-00/7-30 PM. The deceased and her mother did not satisfy his coming and did not allow the presence of the accused. But on her (mother of the deceased) exoneration he was allowed to stay at night with deceased. In this connection, the evidence of PW 1 deposed in his cross that on the fateful night he had been Pabna and come to village two days after occurrence. He did not see the accused staying with deceased at the fateful night at PO house. It is pertinent to mention that except PW 9 none of the witnesses did see the accused stayed with deceased at night at the PO house. PW 9, she stated that on the fateful night the accused stayed with deceased at night and she also stated in his cross examination that at the fateful night PW 9 mother of the deceased had been stayed at the residence of Aziz Khan who was declared tendered by the prosecution. According to PW 9 on the next morning she did not trace out the deceased along with accused and found the bed of the PO house wet. She also stated that witnesses Moklesur and Anisur saw the accused carrying is son Rakibul towards Ambaria village, District-Pabna and after two days the dead body was recovered from garbage near by the ditch at the showing of PW 3 brother-in-law of the deceased. This court did not find the accused in any way involved this offence. Because, taking away the dead body of the deceased by accused from his PO house to a ditch under the garbage about 100/200 hands= 150/300 ft away from the PO house which creates a serious doubt of the prosecution case. Evidence of above prosecution witnesses are very much interested and inter-related required corroboration by independent and impartial witnesses. In the case in hand, there is no independent and impartial witnesses. Moreover, the neighboures may not also come forward to depose in the case. It is not safe to rely on the evidence of highly interested partisan witnesses to earn conviction on a charge without corroboration either ocular or circumstantial. 

 30. It is to be seen that PO house was not searched or visited by the investigating officer and no steps were taken during the investigation to find out any seized alamots. In this connection we may refer to evidence of PW 12 who did not seize any wet earth or cloth from the PO house nor did seize any alamot thereto rendering the prosecution case doubtful. More so, there is no evidence that any incriminating alamots were seized from the place of occurrence by the investigating officer which creates a disbelieve as to the commission of offence in the alleged place of occurrence. In view of the evidence of doctor as PW 4 who clearly deposed that the medical board holding post mortem of the deceased's dead body and could come to a definite opinion that the death was due to asphyxia as a result of throttling which were ante mortem and homicidal in nature. It is well settled that the medical evidence is not substantive evidence within the meaning of section 3 of the Evidence Act. We do not find any independent substantive evidence on record connecting the accused with the commission of offence. Moreover, tendering of vital witness as PW5 Anisur amounts to withholding of material witnesses and non-examination of vital witnesses mentioned in the FIR namely, Moklesur to that effect that had he been examined he would not have supported the prosecution case. As per prosecution claim that Anisur and Moklesur saw the Younus along with his son Rakibul Islam going towards Pabna on 31-12-2006 at 5-30 am. Any way, non-examination of material witnesses shall give rise to a strong presumption against prosecution case and in the instant case presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act shall apply. The learned Tribunal relied upon the evidence of witnesses but PWs 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 were not cross examined by the state defence lawyer. It would be relevant to mention, that the fate of the criminal trial depands upon the truthfulness or otherwise of the witnesses and there-fore, it is of paramount importance. To arrive at the truth, its veracity should be judged and for that purpose cross examination is acid test. We do not find any substantive evidence as there is no eye witnesses against the accused and sup-porting circumstances is absent on evidence on record linking the accused Younus Sarder with the commission of alleged murdered his wife. But taking into account all these facts, the Tribunal come to the conclusion that the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt. We are unable to agree with the view taken by Tribunal rather in this case, it is unsafe to do so grave doubt is, therefore, created as whether the accused could be involved in the offence of wife killing. The reasoning of the Tribunal is totally fallacious. We are, therefore, of the view that benefit of doubt must be given to the accused and he must be acquitted.
